reviewScope: Fresh final-source review of session writers and their workspace/task coordination, separate from the implementation pass; not an external reviewer attestation.

participatingPaths.order: Workspace then Task; newly inserted session/turn are owned by the creating transaction
lockRun before actor/receipt checks and session/turn writes; includes REST and Telegram follow-ups
lockRun in both claim and terminal-result transactions
lockRun in intent and signal-result transactions; final acknowledgment is a separate authorized read
lockRun before final authority/directory/lease checks and any terminal transition
lockRun before lease and interruption/event updates; review found and corrected the remaining session-first path
Candidate discovery is read-only; each mutation transaction calls lockRun
lockRun before durable event append and thread/token metadata updates
Internal helpers called inside the enclosing creation or lockRun transaction
Caller owns the session lock; event sequence/hash and lastSequence update share that transaction

adjacentPaths: Workspace-managed account/role/task mutations acquire the Workspace row first.
Project archival takes its lifecycle advisory lock before Workspace; session execution reads archive state without taking the advisory lock, so no inverse advisory dependency was found.
Project deletion checks active/context session state under Workspace fencing; no separate direct session writer was found outside SessionsService and appendSessionEvent.
History, snapshots and SSE polling use authorized reads rather than SELECT FOR UPDATE.

demonstratedFindings.before: Actual concurrent runner/admission deadlock plus a deterministic physical NOWAIT regression failed before correction
Fresh review found session-only locking; the same physical NOWAIT regression failed on the untouched heartbeat path

regressionDesign: Hold Workspace in an independent transaction, start event or lease persistence, probe the session with FOR UPDATE NOWAIT, then release barriers. This verifies physical lock availability, not merely source/query ordering. Original strict lifecycle and response assertions remain intact.
coverage: existing durable session/deletion and service regressions
limits: This is scoped lock-path review, not a proof that PostgreSQL can never deadlock.
The prior Windows1450 resource incident remains distinct; no host resource setting was changed.
Consistent Workspace serialization can delay heartbeats behind long workspace transactions; no lease duration, timeout or retry policy was changed.
